Wild Animals in Cages - Inside SA Zoos

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Do our municipalities have the resources to manage our zoos effectively?

Unique Selling Point:
Zoos across the country have come under the spotlight as more and more people see them as inhumane and cruel. But although there is an argument for their educational value, the very least they can do is make sure the animals are kept in as comfortable surroundings as possible, and well cared for. While some zoos are managing to provide habitat-simulating enclosures and adequate stimulation, others are housing their menageries in small cages and the condition of the animals says it all.

But who is responsible for the welfare of the animals in our zoos as well as enforcing the law, and how can it be allowed that a brown bear lives in a cement pit for more than three decades?

Summary:
For weeks the debate has raged around Lammie the elephant cow at the Johannesburg Zoo. Her partner died last year and animal welfare organisations are calling for her to be moved to a sanctuary where she can be with other elephants and rewilded to some extent. But the City of Johannesburg is adamant that Lammie will stay at the zoo.

But the issue around whether or not we should have zoos is not clear cut. Some people hail their educational value whilst others see them as cruel and dated. The fact is we still have zoos all over South Africa and our municipalities have a duty to look after the animals in their care.

Last year Bloemfontein Zoo was in the news because of filth and lack of food for the animals. This sparked a campaign against the zoo and municipality, but although the noise has died down, we take a look to see if the animals are truly taken care of. In Gauteng, both the Joburg and Pretoria zoos are commended for their more modern approach to keeping animals. Cages and pit enclosures have been exchanged for habitat-simulating enclosures and for the most part the animals are given "toys" for stimulation. The enclosures are generally kept clean and there doesn't seem to be issues with providing food.

The worst transgressing zoo at the moment seems to be the East London Zoo. Residents, activists and animal welfare organisations have been calling for the zoo's closure for quite some time. Middle last year one of the zoo's brown bears was first spotted with paralysed hind legs - Jenny had been at the zoo, living in a cement pit enclosure for more than 35 years. She was euthanised and now her daughter, Gina is the only remaining bear at the zoo. Witnesses and video footage shows the bear in poor condition, with almost nothing to stimulate her. The water in the moat within her enclosure is filthy.



Further information:
Lammie's case is a complex one. The Zoo says she has attachments to her handlers and will not survive the move, and that the rehabilitation process will do more harm than good. But elephants experts are accusing the zoo of holding on to Lammie for financial reasons, not taking her welfare into account. Along with Lammie's release, animal welfare organisations are calling for the Zoo's closure, saying it is all together inhumane to keep wild animals in enclosures...

But as far as zoos go, Joburg zoo is a pretty nice zoo. Most of the enclosures are of a decent size and mimic the animal's habitat in the wild. Animals are given additional stimuli to entertain themselves... All this is possible because the Joburg Zoo is actually a Not for Profit Company. And although it does receive some funding from the City of Johannesburg, they rely heavily on corporate sponsorship and additional financial assistance. But it is run as a business and is in the business of making money.

Both the Bloemfontein Zoo and the East London Zoo are run by the respective municipalities.

In the case of Bloemfontein, they had difficulties at the end of last year and there was a social media campaign about the conditions at the zoo, but things have died down. The former organisation, Friends of the Bloemfontein Zoo has disbanded and it seems the animals are pretty much forgotten...

In East London the situation is dire.. A lone brown bear, Gina, spends her days in a cement pit. She has been there for 34 years. Her mother Jenny was euthanised last year because her condition deteriorated to such an extent that her hind legs became paralysed. South African Bear Expert, Lionel de Lange who is based in the Ukraine offered to build a bigger enclosure for the 2 bears but although the zoo initially took him up on his offer, they later retracted, saying that De Lange is too keen to speak to journalists. In addition, the zoo has a jaguar in a small wire enclosure. Initially the zoo said it is a temporary home for the animal, but he's been there for almost 18 months! There is also an endangered Cape Vulture in a small cage that does not even give him the luxury of flying. He can barely stretch his wings in his enclosure.

A Campaign to close down the East London Zoo is being run By Algoa FM DJ, Daron Mann.

The NSPCA speaks stongly about the conditions in our municipal zoos. All of our zoos do not comply with international standards. They say zoos have lost experts, there is just about zero stimulation for the animals. There is a lack of discipline amongst the staff, they arrive late for work, feed animals late, lock them up early. There is also not enough staff at the zoos. Zoos are dirty and unkept. Zoos offer very little in educational value. There are only a few posters up and a lonely animal in the cages -- this is not education.

Press Release:


Inside South African Zoos
Zoos are popular facilities where wild animals are locked up in cages and behind glass displays for public entertainment and education. But increasingly international conservation experts are questioning the usefulness and ethics of keeping these animals in captivity. In South Africa, there have been rising reports of animal cruelty in zoos, as municipalities struggle to manage them effectively. Carte Blanche goes inside some of the country’s most controversial menageries.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Watch the trailer


Script:


WILD ANIMALS IN CAGES


V/O
For many South Africans, this is their only opportunity to see an elephant in real life... in a zoo... but more and more people are questioning the value of wild animals in cages.
­Smaragda Louw
Like circuses, the time for zoos have come and gone.
V/O
Smaragda Louw is the director of Ban Animal Trading South Africa, an organisation that is calling for zoos across the country to be closed down.
Smaragda Louw
There are many ways that humans can learn about animals without allowing animals to suffer.
LINK
The debate on whether we should have zoos or not is quite an emotional one. For now though municipalities are adamant that there is value in having zoos, either for education or conservation.
V/O
Municipal zoos are part of our urban recreational and green spaces, and are largely funded by the respective municipalities. This also means that they compete against other more pressing sectors within a city's budget. But when a city chooses to have a zoo as part of it's portfolio the municipality is governed by conservation legislation in terms of things like enclosure size – but they're also obliged to provide the best possible care for the animals according to our Animal Welfare Protection Act. However, senior inspector for the NSPCA, Wendy Wilson, says most of our zoos are not meeting international standards.
Wendy Wilson
Most institutions in South Africa have no formal way or legislated way or standard operating procedure of actually gauging the welfare of the animals in their care.
V/O
In recent months three of our municipal zoos have been in the news because of alleged welfare issues around some of their animals. In East London, the uproar started when one of the zoo's two brown bears was reported to be unwell.
LINK
There has been a huge social media outcry over how animals are being kept at the East London zoo – some people going as far as saying that the zoo should be closed down as no animal should be kept in captivity or in an enclosure.
V/O
These pictures of the bears went viral on social media and in October last year, the one bear was euthanized.
Samkelo
The whole hype around the picture that was circulated at a particular time, I mean it's an interpretation.
V/O
Head of Communications at the Buffalo City Municipality, Samkelo Ngwenya, says the bear was very old.
Samkelo
As far as we're concerned we've done everything by the book to take care of the bear.
V/O
The remaining bear spends her days in a pit, and although the enclosure meets the minimum legal standards, Senior inspector of the NSPCA, Vonny Strachan says it's not enough.
Vonny Strachan
Mac: Is this an ideal environment for a bear? I mean even looking at this one it doesn't look like it's okay.

Definitely not. Animals shouldn't be kept in pits. One, it doesn’t give a good environment for the animal because they've got to constantly look up when there's stimulus coming into the environment.
V/O
Bears are foraging animals, that mostly live high up in the northern hemisphere, so the hot humid climate of the Eastern Cape is not ideal. On top of that there is very little ventilation at the bottom of the pit.
Samkelo
The lifestyle of the bear is okay and we're ensuring that on a daily basis it's needs are being met and it's life is being enriched.
Vonny Strachan
They've basically seen to their needs in terms of food water and shelter. But that's it. And that's what they're legally required to do.The problem is that's not all that it needs.
V/O
But it's not just the bear that has drawn attention at the East London Zoo.
Daron Mann
It's a sad miserable place and it shames us as human beings.
V/O
Algoa FM DJ, Daron Mann is one of the voices calling for the zoo's closure.
Daron Mann
The Jaguar, let's be generous and say he's in an enclosure that's about 40 or 50 square metres – no more than that, and it's archaic.
V/O
Once again the enclosure's size is in line with the law, but it is virtually barren, with very little to occupy the animal.
Vonny Strachan
Just putting that piece of meat on a bungee cord for instance and hanging it from the roof here, that he has to jump and get hold of it, would keep him busy the whole day.
V/O
There is also a lone endangered Cape Vulture in an enclosure, and at first glance it looks to be of a reasonable size... it even has an artificial cliff-side.
Vonny
Being big birds and having wings of almost 2 metres, basically they need too drop to get off the cliff. Now if they'd have to drop he'd either hit the floor or he'd hit the fence.
V/O
So the bird is limited to the occasional wing stretch and when it is not sitting on the beam, it hops around on the floor.
V/O
Ngwenya says that issues around the vulture and jaguar enclosures are being addressed, and that the zoo is constantly improving. In terms of their development plan, they have brought in specialist personnel and are addressing the issues raised by the public and the SPCA.
Samkelo
The status of the zoo is at an improvement stage. It's come from a bad space but it's looking rather very promising.
V/O
At Bloemfontein zoo we met up with inspectors Reinette Meyer and Tebogo Maswanganye from the local SPCA.
Reinette Meyer
Die omgewing is baie vuil, hulle tel nooit die ontlasting van die sebras op nie, dit lyk eintlik terrible.
Tebogo Maswanganye
We have issued warnings to the management that this enclosure needs to be cleaned but nothing happens.
Qondile
Yes there were times when you'd get stories on social media that our cages are not clean.
V/O
Communication Manager at the Mangaung Municipality, Qondile Khedama, says the zoo has it's ups and downs but they are constantly working to improve the facility. Late last year reports on social media surfaced that the zoo did not have enough food for the animals, but Khedama stresses that what you see on social media is not always the truth...
Qondile
There were time when they were saying we do not have enough lucern. And then we had to take out that lucern because there's a period when you need to clean your stores. And then the next thing, when people came to check we had taken back the lucern. And it contradicted what they were saying.
V/O
The Zoo administrators are excited about breeding possibilities in the rhino camp, but Meyer says the conditions don't lend themselves to romantic rendezvous.
Reinette
Dit is dieremishandeling en die dier word heeltemal onreg aangedoen om so aangehou te word.
V/O
The enclosure has no vegetation, except for a few weeds – of which some are even poisonous. But one person's barren, dirty enclosure is another's paradise... it seems...
Qondile
No we're creating a natural scene for animals because if it's too clean you take out the element of nature. So they're natural. It's animals.
V/O
The zoo looks unkempt and run-down, with animal faeces left in enclosures or simply piled next to the footpaths. And despite the recent rains, the waterbodies look filthy. But Khedama insists it's all a matter of perception and says the zoo has adequate skilled staff to look after the animals' particular needs.
Qondile
Generally in terms of skill level, we are very, we're comfortable.
V/O
But the SPCA doesn't agree and says many welfare issues are not being addressed and they are frustrated by continual unheeded warnings.
Reinette
Ons het nou op 'n punt gekom waar ons eintlik 'n docket opstel om hof toe te vat om 'n hofbevel teen die Bloemfontein dieretuin te kry want hierdie is totaal en al onaanvaarbaar wat hier gebeur.
V/O
By comparison, Joburg zoo looks more visitor-friendly than East London and Bloemfontein and spokesperson for Joburg City Parks which manages the zoo, Jenny Moodley, says the joburg facility meets international and local standards.
Jenny Moodley
We aspire to become one of the best zoos in the world. Our animals get one of the best cares in terms of any other zoos across the country. We also know that in terms of animal husbandry we are one of the leaders when it comes to that.
V/O
Lammie, the zoo's lonely elephant cow - is the poster child for a growing public discomfort over whether zoos are able to provide for a wild animal.
LINK
Lammie's enclosure companion, Kinkel passed away last year September and ever since then nature conservationists as well as the NSPCA have called for Lammie to be rehomed in a sanctuary.
Karen Trendler
If you think what an elephant is like in the wild. They're part of a very large herd. They have sophisticated communication, they're intelligent.
V/O
Respected elephant expert, Karen Trendler heads the NSPCA's Wildlife Trade and Trafficking Unit.
Karen Trendler
If you think of the distances they move – on a daily basis they can move up to 60kms and what they're experiencing in their home range and in their environment on a daily basis.
V/O
These are some of the experiences of a wild elephant that the zoo simply cannot recreate. Stimulating her, and keeping her happy, is a full-time job that the zoo is not necessarily geared for, say experts. But the zoo insists this is the best place for her.
Jenny Moodley
She's nurtured here, she's fed as part of a set meal routine, she has an enrichment officer here. So, the support system is right here at the Joburg zoo.
V/O
Moodley does concede that in an ideal world every animal should be free-roaming, but adds that the onslought of wide-scale poaching, growing urbanisation and habitat loss have accelerated the need for zoos. And Lammie, she says, is key to the zoo's environmental education programme.
Jenny Moodley
Through the week we have bus-loads of children that come through here and each one of them stop here at the enclosure, they get to smell the elephant, they get to her about the elephant through the environmental educationalist that are on duty.
Trendler
If you say educational, what are we teaching children? That it's okay to have a single elephant confined.

All three municipalities we visited were quick to point out that zoos play a major role in term,s of education…
Wendy Wilson
Mac: So Wendy, we obviously know all the problems. Why aren't zoos being shut down?

You have to work within the boundaries of legislation. It's a fine line, it's a grey area, you have to prove that that animal over there is a blatant welfare concern.
V/O
For now many insist that our zoos add value to our cities... to education and conservation... but our municipalities need to accept responsibility and prioritise the welfare of the animals in their care.
Wendy Wilson
I think South Africa can actually be quite ashamed of their zoos. And we're a fantastic people, we have a fantastic national heritage. We should be so proud of it. And we're just not doing justice to the animals in this country.


PROMO 1 – 11”
Keeping wild beasts in cages takes a lot more than just adequate food and water. Are municipal zoos equipped to look after all the animals, and provide them with optimal care?


PROMO 2 – 11”
Zoos play a role in environmental education in our cities but at what cost to the animals? Do municipalities have the recourses to ensure the animals live their best lives possible?


PROMO 3 – 11”
Our municipalities have come under fire for the way in which they care for the animals in their zoos. Some people are going as far as to say that the animals should be rehomed in sanctuaries.




































































































V/O
According to Mann the zoo indicated in January 2018 already that it would move the Jaguar to a different enclosure, but to date it still hasn't realised.
Daron Mann
To say that it's a temporary enclosure, acknowledge that it's not good enough, and then a year later he hasn't move, just isn't good enough.

However, senior inspector for the NSPCA, Wendy Wilson, says most of our zoos are not meeting international standards. Wendy Wilson Most institutions in South Africa have no formal way or legislated way or standard operating procedure of actually gauging the welfare of the animals in their care. V/O In recent months three of our municipal zoos have been in the news because of alleged welfare issues around some of their animals. In East London, the uproar started when one of the zoo's two brown bears was reported to be unwell. LINK There has been a huge social media outcry over how animals are being kept at the East London zoo – some people going as far as saying that the zoo should be closed down as no animal should be kept in captivity or in an enclosure. V/O These pictures of the bears went viral on social media and in October last year, the one bear was euthanized. Samkelo The whole hype around the picture that was circulated at a particular time, I mean it's an interpretation. V/O Head of Communications at the Buffalo City Municipality, Samkelo Ngwenya, says the bear was very old. Samkelo As far as we're concerned we've done everything by the book to take care of the bear. V/O The remaining bear spends her days in a pit, and although the enclosure meets the minimum legal standards, Senior inspector of the NSPCA, Vonny Strachan says it's not enough. Vonny Strachan Mac: Is this an ideal environment for a bear? I mean even looking at this one it doesn't look like it's okay. Definitely not. Animals shouldn't be kept in pits. One, it doesn’t give a good environment for the animal because they've got to constantly look up when there's stimulus coming into the environment. V/O Bears are foraging animals, that mostly live high up in the northern hemisphere, so the hot humid climate of the Eastern Cape is not ideal. On top of that there is very little ventilation at the bottom of the pit. Samkelo The lifestyle of the bear is okay and we're ensuring that on a daily basis it's needs are being met and it's life is being enriched. Vonny Strachan They've basically seen to their needs in terms of food water and shelter. But that's it. And that's what they're legally required to do.The problem is that's not all that it needs. V/O But it's not just the bear that has drawn attention at the East London Zoo. Daron Mann It's a sad miserable place and it shames us as human beings. V/O Algoa FM DJ, Daron Mann is one of the voices calling for the zoo's closure. Daron Mann The Jaguar, let's be generous and say he's in an enclosure that's about 40 or 50 square metres – no more than that, and it's archaic. V/O Once again the enclosure's size is in line with the law, but it is virtually barren, with very little to occupy the animal. Vonny Strachan Just putting that piece of meat on a bungee cord for instance and hanging it from the roof here, that he has to jump and get hold of it, would keep him busy the whole day. V/O There is also a lone endangered Cape Vulture in an enclosure, and at first glance it looks to be of a reasonable size... it even has an artificial cliff-side. Vonny Being big birds and having wings of almost 2 metres, basically they need too drop to get off the cliff. Now if they'd have to drop he'd either hit the floor or he'd hit the fence. V/O So the bird is limited to the occasional wing stretch and when it is not sitting on the beam, it hops around on the floor. V/O Ngwenya says that issues around the vulture and jaguar enclosures are being addressed, and that the zoo is constantly improving. In terms of their development plan, they have brought in specialist personnel and are addressing the issues raised by the public and the SPCA. Samkelo The status of the zoo is at an improvement stage. It's come from a bad space but it's looking rather very promising. V/O At Bloemfontein zoo we met up with inspectors Reinette Meyer and Tebogo Maswanganye from the local SPCA. Reinette Meyer Die omgewing is baie vuil, hulle tel nooit die ontlasting van die sebras op nie, dit lyk eintlik terrible. Tebogo Maswanganye We have issued warnings to the management that this enclosure needs to be cleaned but nothing happens. Qondile Yes there were times when you'd get stories on social media that our cages are not clean. V/O Communication Manager at the Mangaung Municipality, Qondile Khedama, says the zoo has it's ups and downs but they are constantly working to improve the facility. Late last year reports on social media surfaced that the zoo did not have enough food for the animals, but Khedama stresses that what you see on social media is not always the truth... Qondile There were time when they were saying we do not have enough lucern. And then we had to take out that lucern because there's a period when you need to clean your stores. And then the next thing, when people came to check we had taken back the lucern. And it contradicted what they were saying. V/O The Zoo administrators are excited about breeding possibilities in the rhino camp, but Meyer says the conditions don't lend themselves to romantic rendezvous. Reinette Dit is dieremishandeling en die dier word heeltemal onreg aangedoen om so aangehou te word. V/O The enclosure has no vegetation, except for a few weeds – of which some are even poisonous. But one person's barren, dirty enclosure is another's paradise... it seems... Qondile No we're creating a natural scene for animals because if it's too clean you take out the element of nature. So they're natural. It's animals. V/O The zoo looks unkempt and run-down, with animal faeces left in enclosures or simply piled next to the footpaths. And despite the recent rains, the waterbodies look filthy. But Khedama insists it's all a matter of perception and says the zoo has adequate skilled staff to look after the animals' particular needs. Qondile Generally in terms of skill level, we are very, we're comfortable. V/O But the SPCA doesn't agree and says many welfare issues are not being addressed and they are frustrated by continual unheeded warnings. Reinette Ons het nou op 'n punt gekom waar ons eintlik 'n docket opstel om hof toe te vat om 'n hofbevel teen die Bloemfontein dieretuin te kry want hierdie is totaal en al onaanvaarbaar wat hier gebeur. V/O By comparison, Joburg zoo looks more visitor-friendly than East London and Bloemfontein and spokesperson for Joburg City Parks which manages the zoo, Jenny Moodley, says the joburg facility meets international and local standards. Jenny Moodley We aspire to become one of the best zoos in the world. Our animals get one of the best cares in terms of any other zoos across the country. We also know that in terms of animal husbandry we are one of the leaders when it comes to that. V/O Lammie, the zoo's lonely elephant cow - is the poster child for a growing public discomfort over whether zoos are able to provide for a wild animal. LINK Lammie's enclosure companion, Kinkel passed away last year September and ever since then nature conservationists as well as the NSPCA have called for Lammie to be rehomed in a sanctuary. Karen Trendler If you think what an elephant is like in the wild. They're part of a very large herd. They have sophisticated communication, they're intelligent. V/O Respected elephant expert, Karen Trendler heads the NSPCA's Wildlife Trade and Trafficking Unit. Karen Trendler If you think of the distances they move – on a daily basis they can move up to 60kms and what they're experiencing in their home range and in their environment on a daily basis. V/O These are some of the experiences of a wild elephant that the zoo simply cannot recreate. Stimulating her, and keeping her happy, is a full-time job that the zoo is not necessarily geared for, say experts. But the zoo insists this is the best place for her. Jenny Moodley She's nurtured here, she's fed as part of a set meal routine, she has an enrichment officer here. So, the support system is right here at the Joburg zoo. V/O Moodley does concede that in an ideal world every animal should be free-roaming, but adds that the onslought of wide-scale poaching, growing urbanisation and habitat loss have accelerated the need for zoos. And Lammie, she says, is key to the zoo's environmental education programme. Jenny Moodley Through the week we have bus-loads of children that come through here and each one of them stop here at the enclosure, they get to smell the elephant, they get to her about the elephant through the environmental educationalist that are on duty. Trendler If you say educational, what are we teaching children? That it's okay to have a single elephant confined. All three municipalities we visited were quick to point out that zoos play a major role in term,s of education… Wendy Wilson Mac: So Wendy, we obviously know all the problems. Why aren't zoos being shut down? You have to work within the boundaries of legislation. It's a fine line, it's a grey area, you have to prove that that animal over there is a blatant welfare concern. V/O For now many insist that our zoos add value to our cities... to education and conservation... but our municipalities need to accept responsibility and prioritise the welfare of the animals in their care. Wendy Wilson I think South Africa can actually be quite ashamed of their zoos. And we're a fantastic people, we have a fantastic national heritage. We should be so proud of it. And we're just not doing justice to the animals in this country. PROMO 1 – 11” Keeping wild beasts in cages takes a lot more than just adequate food and water. Are municipal zoos equipped to look after all the animals, and provide them with optimal care? PROMO 2 – 11” Zoos play a role in environmental education in our cities but at what cost to the animals? Do municipalities have the recourses to ensure the animals live their best lives possible? PROMO 3 – 11” Our municipalities have come under fire for the way in which they care for the animals in their zoos. Some people are going as far as to say that the animals should be rehomed in sanctuaries. V/O According to Mann the zoo indicated in January 2018 already that it would move the Jaguar to a different enclosure, but to date it still hasn't realised. Daron Mann To say that it's a temporary enclosure, acknowledge that it's not good enough, and then a year later he hasn't move, just isn't good enough.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Do our municipalities have the resources to manage our zoos effectively?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Zoos across the country have come under the spotlight as more and more people see them as inhumane and cruel. But although there is an argument for their educational value, the very least they can do is make sure the animals are kept in as comfortable surroundings as possible, and well cared for. While some zoos are managing to provide habitat-simulating enclosures and adequate stimulation, others are housing their menageries in small cages and the condition of the animals says it all. But who is responsible for the welfare of the animals in our zoos as well as enforcing the law, and how can it be allowed that a brown bear lives in a cement pit for more than three decades?
metadata.Summary: For weeks the debate has raged around Lammie the elephant cow at the Johannesburg Zoo. Her partner died last year and animal welfare organisations are calling for her to be moved to a sanctuary where she can be with other elephants and rewilded to some extent. But the City of Johannesburg is adamant that Lammie will stay at the zoo. But the issue around whether or not we should have zoos is not clear cut. Some people hail their educational value whilst others see them as cruel and dated. The fact is we still have zoos all over South Africa and our municipalities have a duty to look after the animals in their care. Last year Bloemfontein Zoo was in the news because of filth and lack of food for the animals. This sparked a campaign against the zoo and municipality, but although the noise has died down, we take a look to see if the animals are truly taken care of. In Gauteng, both the Joburg and Pretoria zoos are commended for their more modern approach to keeping animals. Cages and pit enclosures have been exchanged for habitat-simulating enclosures and for the most part the animals are given "toys" for stimulation. The enclosures are generally kept clean and there doesn't seem to be issues with providing food. The worst transgressing zoo at the moment seems to be the East London Zoo. Residents, activists and animal welfare organisations have been calling for the zoo's closure for quite some time. Middle last year one of the zoo's brown bears was first spotted with paralysed hind legs - Jenny had been at the zoo, living in a cement pit enclosure for more than 35 years. She was euthanised and now her daughter, Gina is the only remaining bear at the zoo. Witnesses and video footage shows the bear in poor condition, with almost nothing to stimulate her. The water in the moat within her enclosure is filthy.
metadata.Further information: Lammie's case is a complex one. The Zoo says she has attachments to her handlers and will not survive the move, and that the rehabilitation process will do more harm than good. But elephants experts are accusing the zoo of holding on to Lammie for financial reasons, not taking her welfare into account. Along with Lammie's release, animal welfare organisations are calling for the Zoo's closure, saying it is all together inhumane to keep wild animals in enclosures... But as far as zoos go, Joburg zoo is a pretty nice zoo. Most of the enclosures are of a decent size and mimic the animal's habitat in the wild. Animals are given additional stimuli to entertain themselves... All this is possible because the Joburg Zoo is actually a Not for Profit Company. And although it does receive some funding from the City of Johannesburg, they rely heavily on corporate sponsorship and additional financial assistance. But it is run as a business and is in the business of making money. Both the Bloemfontein Zoo and the East London Zoo are run by the respective municipalities. In the case of Bloemfontein, they had difficulties at the end of last year and there was a social media campaign about the conditions at the zoo, but things have died down. The former organisation, Friends of the Bloemfontein Zoo has disbanded and it seems the animals are pretty much forgotten... In East London the situation is dire.. A lone brown bear, Gina, spends her days in a cement pit. She has been there for 34 years. Her mother Jenny was euthanised last year because her condition deteriorated to such an extent that her hind legs became paralysed. South African Bear Expert, Lionel de Lange who is based in the Ukraine offered to build a bigger enclosure for the 2 bears but although the zoo initially took him up on his offer, they later retracted, saying that De Lange is too keen to speak to journalists. In addition, the zoo has a jaguar in a small wire enclosure. Initially the zoo said it is a temporary home for the animal, but he's been there for almost 18 months! There is also an endangered Cape Vulture in a small cage that does not even give him the luxury of flying. He can barely stretch his wings in his enclosure. A Campaign to close down the East London Zoo is being run By Algoa FM DJ, Daron Mann. The NSPCA speaks stongly about the conditions in our municipal zoos. All of our zoos do not comply with international standards. They say zoos have lost experts, there is just about zero stimulation for the animals. There is a lack of discipline amongst the staff, they arrive late for work, feed animals late, lock them up early. There is also not enough staff at the zoos. Zoos are dirty and unkept. Zoos offer very little in educational value. There are only a few posters up and a lonely animal in the cages -- this is not education.
